# V4.1 single-user HBM region and service candidate

**Status: candidate for architecture review.** The executable ledger is `results/arch/v41_single_user_region_candidate.json`, generated by `tools/v41_single_user_region_candidate.py` from source-pinned RTL, technology and budget files. Nothing in this document configures the die or proves an end-to-end token rate. `--require-service` exits 2 while the interfaces remain unconnected.

All addresses below are **32-byte sector offsets within each physical HBM3E stack**; each interval is `[start_sector, end_sector_exclusive)`. The sector limit is 703,125,000 physical and 632,812,500 under the adopted 0.9 reserve. One 1M RoPE table occupies 2,097,152 sectors per stack; both plain and YaRN occupy 4,194,304 sectors. These tables remain full-size even at a 200K run because the current guard uses `ROPE_MAX_POS=1,048,576`.

## Candidate placement

One ratio-1 layer die owns a quarter of the source rows. Index keys are assigned to four stacks in 16-key groups by `global_key[5:4]`; the address module uses 2,176-sector superblocks for each 1,024 stack-local keys. The 200K partial tail reaches sector 26,664 but the simple region reserves 28,288 sectors. At 1M, the 65,536 stack-local keys reserve 139,264 sectors. The packed window occupies 2,176 sectors on stack 0 only. Selected FP4 CKV would occupy nine sectors per row, with `source_id[7:6]` choosing a stack and `source_id[5:4]` choosing a die. Its proposed local row stride yields 112,500 sectors per stack at 200K and 589,824 at 1M. The selected CKV DMA is standalone and **not connected** to the die.

In the ROM candidate, on-die weights use no HBM weight region. In the comparator candidate, the model's 5.154 GB of weights per comparator die is provisionally divided equally among the four stacks, **40,268,784 sectors per stack**. This is a capacity reservation to expose the missing service; the current hardware has a separate W memory on stack 0 and cannot perform the proposed stripe.

The die does not currently forward `W_HBM` to the tile, whose default is `W_HBM=1`. The ROM path therefore also needs a die-level mode binding to the tested ROM tile service before a matched die A/B can run.

| Context | Mode | Stack 0 end | Each other stack end | Sector reserve verdict |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|
| 200K | ROM | 4,337,268 | 4,335,092 | fits one user |
| 200K | HBM comparator | 44,606,052 | 44,603,876 | fits one user if the provisional weight stripe is built |
| 1M | ROM | 4,925,568 | 4,923,392 | fits one user |
| 1M | HBM comparator | 45,194,352 | 45,192,176 | fits one user if the provisional weight stripe is built |

The JSON ledger enumerates every region and bound for each stack. Fitting one user does not establish the modeled hundreds or thousands of users: the current die has only a compile-time key slice, default single-user region parameters and no CKV placement. It also does not prove that 0.9 capacity is available after controller metadata and allocation granularity.

## Concurrent service contract to prove

- **Indexer:** B side of the 32 pseudo-channel K arbiter. Keys use the sharded reader/writer pair, with `pc_of(sector)` choosing the pseudo-channel. The die currently leaves `IDX_SHARDED=0`, so it does not use this candidate.
- **Window, selected CKV and RoPE:** one shared K request per stack through `ot_chip_v41x_kv_rope_reqmux`, then the B/K arbiter. The window module is connected on stack 0; the CKV mux request is currently tied to zero. The mux uses owner tags to route responses, and the per-PC arbiter alternates B and K requests under contention. RoPE has no separate HBM port.
- **Comparator weights:** the present QE qstream is a separate eight-PC W-port model on **stack 0**. It is not part of the K-port physical capacity or arbitration. The tile emits an AW30 `wq_addr` but the die narrows it to `[23:0]`, and qstream itself is fixed to HAW24. Even one provisionally striped stack's weight region requires over 40 million sectors, beyond 24 bits. An exact shared physical weight service and a wide address are required before a comparator die claim.

Root architecture review must choose the actual ROM and comparator region bases and weight service, then bind the approved configuration into the die and image builder. The ledger's `acceptance_checks` name the minimal address-boundary, two-client and all-client exact gates. Physical P&R and source-pinned full-token ROM/HBM runs follow those service gates.
